about_page_description: Game audio student at DAE. 12 years of piano, 4 shipped games, and a growing pile of scripts that fix things Wwise breaks.
intro_sub: 22 · Belgium · Third-year @ DAE Howest · EU passport
story_1: I played piano for 12 years, since I was six. At some point in high school I got more interested in how sound actually works than in performing. Went from music theory to physics and maths, started messing with Python to fix broken audio files.
story_2: At DAE I ended up building a beatbox classifier because the existing ML models were too slow for what I needed. Wrote some Wwise scripts too - got tired of manually fixing references after every Perforce merge. Did audio for 4 student games in Wwise, MetaSounds and FMOD.
story_3: My thesis is about whether AI can do real-time game audio. It can't yet, but I got a caching system working that delivers sounds in under 55 ms - good enough for most gameplay situations.
affiliations_intro: Places where I studied, collaborated, researched, or contributed across game audio, XR, and interactive media.
approach_1: I usually start from whatever's broken - wrong surface on footsteps, a SoundBank using way too much memory. You figure out what actually matters when things go wrong.
approach_2: If I catch myself doing the same thing twice I'll write a script for it. The Wwise repair tool started that way, now the whole team uses it. Same with the UE Rebuilder.
approach_3: Working on student games with 4-player split screen taught me a lot about cutting audio down to what's actually needed. Not everything deserves a spot in the mix.
cta_text: Game audio, 3-6 months, 2026. EU passport, happy to relocate.
stat_mix_detail: Mixing, mastering, sound design - if it's top-shelf, I've tried it
stat_people_detail: I like connecting people and talking shop
